name: Smith flat press
cue: Lower the bar to your mid chest, then press straight up.
research: The Smith incline press (incline_press.json) with a flat bench: Smith machine, bench at 0 deg (one flat pad through the back landmarks, trunk -90 = lying level, the legs keep the incline press stance: hips 15, knees 100, shins vertical, feet flat on a foot plate), bar on vertical rails 0.36 H out (just outside the sleeves, plates outboard). The bar touches the mid chest (the sternal pec, thorax rest point y 0.72, skin 0.004 H under the bar) and rises 0.24 H (43 cm) straight up to a soft lockout (elbow 14). Grip x 0.175 H each side (~1.5x biacromial, hands just outside the shoulders, science audit A12). Rails stand 0.205 H toward the feet from the shoulder joints, i.e. over the lower chest, so the forearms lean a little at the lockout. The hands are solved by IK to the bar with a fixed pole (elbows out and down, flare 52 at the bottom, 26 at the top; humerus 36 deg behind the frontal plane at the touch, 64 deg in front at the lockout), the scapulae retracted and depressed as in the incline (clav pro -14 -> -10, elev -8 -> -5). Flat bench: more mid chest, less upper chest than the incline (the sternal pec glows, the front delts are the amber secondary; the triceps are not drawn: a detached oval on the lateral upper arm, as in the chest press). The back pad is 0.186 H above the floor (hip 0.251); the back landmarks lie within 0.012 H of it (sacrum 0.012 into the pad, thorax 0.002, occiput 0.005).

targets.note: Bar touches the mid chest with elbows ~133 and the humerus ~36 deg behind the frontal plane (the chest skin sets the bottom), soft lockout elbow ~14; plane and elbow keep the incline press tolerance for the mid-press path.

camera.note: Research view az 80 / el 10 (profile: the vertical bar path). Raised 25 deg and turned 10 deg toward the front (az 70 / el 35, 27 deg off the research view): the chest faces up, so the higher lens reads the pec under the bar, and the near plate and rail project below the bench instead of across the head (from az 56 / el 29 the near plate covered the head at the bottom). The bench stands on two feet and a centre rail, with a foot plate under the feet only, so the floor under the name stays clear.
